title: The Phoenix Mills Ltd - 503100 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Phoenix Mills FY26 consolidated revenue rose 16% to Rs 4,423 crore and EBITDA 22% to Rs 2,637 crore, with no new retail capacity added.
summary.overview: FY26 showed strong broad-based growth: consolidated revenue Rs 4,423 crore (+16%), EBITDA Rs 2,637 crore (+22%), and PAT Rs 1,557 crore (+20%), achieved without adding retail area. Retail consumption hit a record Rs 16,587 crore (+21%), with Q4 up 31%, though retail rentals grew only 10% to Rs 2,157 crore, which management attributes to the MG-plus-revenue-share lease structure and ramp-up of newer malls. Offices expanded to 4.8 million sq ft with occupancy at 70%, and management expects a meaningful step-up in office income from FY27. Net debt to EBITDA improved to 1.19x despite the ISMDPL (CPP stake) buyout and peak construction capex.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating free cash flow (after WC, tax, interest)

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Rental income Rs 2,157 crore (+10%) and EBITDA Rs 2,246 crore (+12%); consumption Rs 16,587 crore (+21%), Q4 consumption +31%. Phoenix Palladium rent Rs 461 crore (+14%).

segments.name: Office
segments.commentary: Operational Mumbai and Pune office income Rs 213 crore with EBITDA about Rs 141 crore; portfolio 4.8 million sq ft, occupancy 70%, gross leasing over 2.2 million sq ft in FY26.

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Income Rs 596 crore (+8%), EBITDA Rs 276 crore (+14%); St Regis Mumbai EBITDA margin 49%, average room rate above Rs 21,000.

segments.name: Residential
segments.commentary: Gross bookings Rs 471 crore (doubled), collections Rs 467 crore, revenue recognised Rs 489 crore; realisations about Rs 28,000-29,000 per sq ft in Bengaluru projects.

guidance_outlook: Retail: strong double-digit rental growth expected for Phoenix Market City Pune (about 14-15%) and Bangalore (about 20%) in FY27; management expects sustained double-digit retail earnings growth over the next phase.

Office: occupancy to progress towards 90% over the next few quarters; quarterly office income expected to double from current levels by Q4 FY27; meaningful step-up in rental income and EBITDA from FY27.
Trading occupancy at Phoenix Market City Pune and Bangalore to reach about 90% by end Q1 FY27 and 95-96% by end FY27.
Kolkata (Phoenix Grand Victoria) and Surat malls targeted to open in H2 FY28; Kolkata residential launch timeline to be updated in coming quarters.
April 2026 retail consumption growth close to 30%, or 17-18% excluding jewellery and electronics.
capex_capacity: Invested about Rs 1,035 crore in construction and development across retail and office, plus Rs 431 crore in land and development rights in FY26.
Thane: environmental clearance received, excavation contractor onboarded, excavation to start shortly.
Coimbatore: approvals in place, excavation commenced in Q4 FY26.
Chandigarh: approvals obtained, pre-construction works initiated.
Phoenix Grand Victoria, Kolkata 79% leased; Phoenix Surat 41% leased; both targeted operational in FY28.
Pipeline extended through 2030 to around 18 million sq ft; new city transactions (Hyderabad, Jaipur, Navi Mumbai scouted) targeted for one or two announcements in FY27.
demand_pricing: FY26 leasing about 920 deals covering 3.2 million sq ft; about 2 million sq ft in the operational portfolio at a blended new-and-renewal rental uplift of nearly 20%.
Over 400 new stores opened in FY26, including Apple, Ikea, Uniqlo, Bershka, Rolex and Tanishq.
Fashion and accessories (about 60% of area) grew 16%; cinema and entertainment +22%; jewellery and electronics grew over 30%.
Consumption ex-jewellery and electronics: 14-15% for FY26, about 16% in Q3 and about 18% in Q4.
Rent-to-consumption at new malls normalising to a portfolio average of about 10-11%; about 90% of rental income treated as fixed by management.

Office tenant demand described as strong; several deals in pipeline with commercials closed and documentation under way. RISE Commercial talks with IPCs at an advanced stage; no pre-leasing disclosed yet.
Bangalore office about 33% leased per analyst, management cites late 30s leased occupancy with pipeline for a substantial increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q4 consumption growth excluding jewellery and electronics, and how will the rent-consumption gap move in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-jewellery and electronics, Q4 consumption growth was about 17-18%. Management expects the gap to narrow as revenue share kicks in, and says rental growth should hold even if jewellery and electronics moderate.

qa_highlights.question: Will the PMC Pune and Bangalore consumption gains reflect in rentals, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9% of area in both malls is leased but not yet trading, so rental upside lands in FY27; Pune is seen at 14-15% rental upside and Bangalore about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What rental upside is expected from the roughly 50% of portfolio area expiring in the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for rental uplift similar to FY26's roughly 20% blended new and renewal growth, supported by brand repositioning and F&B concepts like Gourmet Village; market conditions must remain supportive.

qa_highlights.question: When will office rental income start and how fast will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue from newer office assets expected from Q2 FY27, growing quarter on quarter, with quarterly office income seen doubling by Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consumption trend in April 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: April is very strong, with close to 30% growth including Akshay Tritiya; excluding jewellery and electronics, growth would be about 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the land strategy beyond 2030 and for new cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Scouting Hyderabad, Jaipur and Navi Mumbai; one or two new-city transactions targeted in FY27, plus conversion of existing assets such as Palladium and PMC Bangalore into super campuses.

risks_watch: Retail rental growth (10%) lagging consumption growth (21%); convergence depends on revenue share kicking in and jewellery/electronics mix.
Reliance on jewellery and electronics for consumption momentum, which carry low revenue share ratios.
Trading occupancy ramp-up at PMC Pune and Bangalore to 90% by end Q1 FY27 and 95-96% by end FY27.
Office occupancy at 70% overall, with Bangalore leased in the late 30s; RISE Commercial pre-leasing yet to be disclosed.
Kolkata residential launch timeline still pending; Kolkata and Surat malls in H2 FY28.
Macro volatility noted by analysts; management described hotel backdrop as challenging.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on retail and office leasing momentum, with specific numeric guidance for FY27 rental uplift. More measured on timelines for Kolkata residential and RISE pre-leasing, and declined to split minimum guarantee from revenue share income.
key_quotes: Importantly, we delivered this performance without adding any new retail capacity during the year.
Even as Q4 consumption moderated sequentially, retail rentals remained largely stable and retail EBITDA was essentially flat quarter-on-quarter.

We typically don't provide that breakup, Parikshit but you may consider 90% of the rental income to be fixed in nature and the rest is incremental revenue share over and above the fixed rent that we generate from retailers.
We will come back and make those disclosures, Mohit, the minute we start signing LOIs.

growth.why: Management guides mid-to-high double-digit retail rental growth in FY27 (PMC Pune ~14-15%, Bangalore ~20%) and office income doubling by Q4 FY27, backed by leasing (920 deals, 3.2 mn sq ft), trading occupancy targets of 90% by end Q1 FY27 and 95-96% by end FY27, and new malls only in H2 FY28, with no new retail area added in FY26 and about 70% office occupancy.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Office income expected to double by Q4 FY27 from Q2 FY27 onwards, and retail rental growth of 14-15% at Pune and about 20% at Bangalore should lift EBITDA faster than costs, after FY26 EBITDA grew 22% on revenue up 16%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new retail area was added in FY26 and the Kolkata and Surat malls only open in H2 FY28, so no new retail capacity lands in the window; office growth comes from leasing up existing 4.8 mn sq ft.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Retail consumption grew 21% to Rs 16,587 crore in FY26 with Q4 at +31% and April near 30%, and trading occupancy at PMC Pune and Bangalore is targeted at 90% by end Q1 FY27 and 95-96% by end FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 70% on the 4.8 mn sq ft office portfolio and retail area is not being expanded, but management plans one or two new-city transactions (Hyderabad, Jaipur, Navi Mumbai) in FY27, and Rs 1,035 crore of construction capex was spent in FY26.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides mid-to-high double-digit retail rental growth in FY27, and April consumption near 30% (17-18% ex jewellery and electronics) could push rentals above that if the revenue share kicks in faster than expected.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rental growth of 10% trails consumption growth of 21%, and reliance on jewellery and electronics, which have low revenue-share ratios, could hold rentals back if those categories moderate.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Over 400 new stores opened in FY26 including Apple, Ikea and Uniqlo, and F&B concepts like Gourmet Village are being used to reposition brands at expiring leases covering about 50% of area over 2-3 years.

rows.label: Office leasing pipeline and RISE Commercial pre-leasing
rows.why: FY26 gross leasing was over 2.2 mn sq ft and several deals have commercials closed with documentation under way, though RISE Commercial pre-leasing is not yet disclosed and Bangalore is only in the late 30s % leased.

rows.label: New city transactions (Hyderabad, Jaipur, Navi Mumbai)
rows.why: Management targets one or two new-city announcements in FY27 after scouting, and the pipeline has been extended through 2030 to about 18 mn sq ft.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA below 1.2x despite ISMDPL buyout
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.19x from 1.24x last year, with net debt at Rs 3,160 crore after the ISMDPL buyout and peak construction capex.

tone.note: Management was confident on retail consumption, April trading near 30%, and specific FY27 rental uplift numbers (Pune 14-15%, Bangalore ~20%), but measured on Kolkata residential timing, RISE pre-leasing, and declined to split minimum guarantee from revenue share; analysts pushed on the rent-consump
